body.statement: For \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\) along even \(n\), the constructed family is nondegenerate and satisfies \(\mathcal L_n=\{\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}:\boldsymbol\vartheta\in\Theta_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\}\subset\mathcal C_n\). Under every \(\mathbb P_{\boldsymbol\vartheta,n}\), \(X_n\sim N(\boldsymbol\vartheta,\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}})\) conditionally on \(\mathcal F_n\), where \(\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) is independent of \(\boldsymbol\vartheta\), \(s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^2=\sigma_n^2(3/n+6/n^2)\), and the independent direct lead-response share equals \((3+6/n)^{-1}\) for every \(\ell\le H_n\).
body.justification: This proposition supplies the legal fixed-covariance location experiment required by the centered-width argument.
body.gap: The persistent rank-one calculation fixes its mean path and therefore cannot itself support an honesty infimum over a nondegenerate location parameter.
body.consumer: It makes the direct-width certificate auditable as a restriction of the declared TWSF class rather than as an external Gaussian comparison experiment.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a sufficiently large even \(n\), condition on \(\mathcal F_n\), and abbreviate \(H=H_n\), \(\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol 1_n\), \(\boldsymbol v=\boldsymbol v_n\), and \(h_\ell=(-1)^\ell\).  By the definition of \(\boldsymbol v_n\),
\[
 \boldsymbol u^{\top}\boldsymbol v=0,
 \qquad \|\boldsymbol u\|_2^2=\|\boldsymbol v\|_2^2=n.
\]
Let
\[
 P=\frac{\boldsymbol u\boldsymbol u^{\top}+\boldsymbol v\boldsymbol v^{\top}}{n}
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 B_n=\boldsymbol u\boldsymbol u^{\top}+\boldsymbol v\boldsymbol v^{\top}=nP.
\]
Thus \(P\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{span}\{\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v\}\), \(B_n\) has rank two, both its nonzero singular values equal \(n\), and
\[
 B_n^\dagger=\frac{P}{n}
 =\frac{\boldsymbol u\boldsymbol u^{\top}+\boldsymbol v\boldsymbol v^{\top}}{n^2}.
\]
Consequently the minimum-norm coefficients in the frozen definitions are
\[
 \beta_n=\frac{\cos(\varphi)\boldsymbol u+\sin(\varphi)\boldsymbol v}{n},
 \qquad
 a_{n,\ell}=\frac{\boldsymbol u+h_\ell\boldsymbol v}{n},
 \qquad
 a_n=\frac{\boldsymbol u-\boldsymbol v}{n}.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \|\beta_n\|_2^2=\frac1n,
 \qquad
 a_{n,\ell}^{\top}a_{n,k}=\frac{1+h_\ell h_k}{n},
 \qquad
 \|a_n\|_2^2=\frac2n.
\]

We first verify membership in \(\mathcal C_n\).  The two deterministic factor coordinates \(1\) and \((-1)^j\), with unit loading vector \((1,(-1)^i)^{\top}\) at row \(i\), give
\[
 B_n(i,j)=1+(-1)^{i+j}.
\]
The target loading \((\cos(\varphi),\sin(\varphi))^{\top}\) gives \(\bar y_n(\varphi)=\cos(\varphi)\boldsymbol u+\sin(\varphi)\boldsymbol v\) and the future means
\[
 \theta_{n,\ell}=\cos(\varphi)+h_\ell\sin(\varphi).
\]
This is an explicit realization of the invariant-unit factor condition \(\mathrm{ass{:}factor\mbox{-}model}\).  Each of the two temporal factor coordinates has Hankel rank one, so the fixed Hankel-rank condition holds.  All five panel dimensions equal \(n\), all displayed signal matrices have rank two and nonzero singular values \(n\), and their entries, the response means, and the target means are bounded in absolute value by \(2\).  Hence the balanced-dimension, fixed-rank, strong-spectrum, and bounded-mean conditions hold with the fixed class envelopes containing this displayed rank-two construction.

Because
\[
 \operatorname{col}(B_n)=\operatorname{span}\{\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v\}
 =\operatorname{col}(B_n^{\top}),
\]
the unit-recovery condition holds.  Moreover,
\[
 B_na_{n,\ell}=\boldsymbol u+h_\ell\boldsymbol v,
 \qquad
 B_na_n=\boldsymbol u-\boldsymbol v,
\]
so every direct response belongs to the selected temporal column space.  The direct terminal-transport equality is verified rather than assumed:
\[
 a_{n,\ell}^{\top}\bar W_n^{\top}\beta_n
 =a_{n,\ell}^{\top}B_n\beta_n
 =\frac{(\boldsymbol u+h_\ell\boldsymbol v)^{\top}
 (\cos(\varphi)\boldsymbol u+\sin(\varphi)\boldsymbol v)}{n}
 =\cos(\varphi)+h_\ell\sin(\varphi)
 =\theta_{n,\ell}.
\]
For recursive recovery, every valid recurrence for the two factor sequences advances the constant coordinate to the constant coordinate and the alternating coordinate to its sign-flipped value.  Every advanced population terminal state therefore remains in \(\operatorname{span}\{\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v\}=\operatorname{col}(\bar Z_{\mathrm{rec},n})\), as required by \(\mathrm{ass{:}recursive\mbox{-}recovery}\).

The minimum-norm recurrence also directly verifies short-horizon stability.  Write \(A=\Pi_n(a_n)=S_n+e_na_n^{\top}\).  Since \(n\) is even,
\[
 a_n^{\top}\boldsymbol u=1,
 \qquad a_n^{\top}\boldsymbol v=-1,
 \qquad S_n\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol u-e_n,
 \qquad S_n\boldsymbol v=-\boldsymbol v+e_n,
\]
and hence \(A\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol u\) and \(A\boldsymbol v=-\boldsymbol v\).  Also \(\|S_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\) and \(\|e_na_n^{\top}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sqrt{2/n}\), whence, for \(0\le j\le H\),
\[
 \|A^j\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le (1+\sqrt{2/n})^j
 \le \exp(\sqrt2 H/\sqrt n)
 \le \exp(\sqrt2),
\]
where the last inequality uses \(H=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\le\sqrt n\).  Thus the stable-short-recursion condition holds with a constant independent of \(n\).

The training menus are singletons, so their measurable selections are deterministic.  The stipulated disjoint observed blocks and the i.i.d. Gaussian-cell construction give, respectively, independent selection, the required block independence, and conditionally i.i.d. \(N(0,\sigma_n^2)\) primitive errors; the declared noise-scale condition supplies \(0<c_\sigma\le\sigma_n\le C_\sigma\).

It remains to verify the variance floor and calculate the direct covariance.  The population direct Riesz loadings reduce to
\[
 p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}
 =B_n^{\dagger\top}B_na_{n,\ell}=a_{n,\ell},
 \qquad
 q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}
 =B_n^{\dagger\top}B_n^{\top}\beta_n=\beta_n.
\]
For recursion, if \(g_{n,\ell}=(A^\ell)^{\top}e_n\), then
\[
 \boldsymbol u^{\top}g_{n,\ell}=e_n^{\top}A^\ell\boldsymbol u=1,
 \qquad
 \boldsymbol v^{\top}g_{n,\ell}=e_n^{\top}A^\ell\boldsymbol v=h_\ell.
\]
It follows that
\[
 p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}
 =B_n^{\dagger\top}B_ng_{n,\ell}
 =Pg_{n,\ell}
 =\frac{\boldsymbol u+h_\ell\boldsymbol v}{n},
 \qquad \|p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}\|_2^2=\frac2n.
\]
The disjoint Gaussian response term \(p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^{\top}e_{y,n}\) is one summand of the recursive score, so independence of the primitive blocks yields
\[
 s_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}^2\ge
 \sigma_n^2\|p_{\mathrm{rec},n,\ell}\|_2^2
 =\frac{2\sigma_n^2}{n}.
\]
The direct variance computed below is at least \(3\sigma_n^2/n\).  Together with \(\sigma_n\ge c_\sigma\), these inequalities verify the stated \(n^{-1/2}\) marginal variance floor.

For two direct leads \(\ell,k\), expand the score from \(\mathrm{def{:}stacked\mbox{-}scores}\).  The Gaussian-cell and disjoint-block conditions imply that the terminal, unit-regression, and temporal-regression blocks are mutually independent; distinct direct response errors are also independent, whereas the same \(E_{Z,\mathrm{dir},n}\) is shared across leads.  Therefore
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Cov}(G_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell},G_{\mathrm{dir},n,k}
 \mid\mathcal F_n)}{\sigma_n^2}
 =\|\beta_n\|_2^2a_{n,\ell}^{\top}a_{n,k}
 +(1+\|\beta_n\|_2^2)p_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^{\top}p_{\mathrm{dir},n,k}
 +\|q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\|_2^2
 \{\mathbf 1\{\ell=k\}+a_{n,\ell}^{\top}a_{n,k}\}.
\]
Substitution of the preceding identities gives the explicit covariance
\[
 \frac{\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\ell,k)}{\sigma_n^2}
 =\left(1+\frac3n\right)\frac{1+h_\ell h_k}{n}
 +\frac{\mathbf 1\{\ell=k\}}{n}.
\]
This expression is independent of \(\varphi\), and its diagonal is
\[
 s_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^2
 =\sigma_n^2\left(\frac3n+\frac6{n^2}\right).
\]
The last diagonal term is precisely the contribution \(q_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}^{\top}e_{\mathrm{dir},n,\ell}\).  Its variance is \(\sigma_n^2\|\beta_n\|_2^2=\sigma_n^2/n\), and these contributions are independent over \(\ell\) and independent of all remaining score terms.  Its standardized variance share is consequently
\[
 \frac{\sigma_n^2/n}{\sigma_n^2(3/n+6/n^2)}=\frac1{3+6/n}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}
 =\frac{\sigma_n^2}{n}I_H
 +\frac{\sigma_n^2(1+3/n)}{n}
 \bigl(\boldsymbol 1_H\boldsymbol 1_H^{\top}
 +\boldsymbol h_n\boldsymbol h_n^{\top}\bigr)
 \succeq \frac{\sigma_n^2}{n}I_H,
\]
so the covariance is positive definite.  Conditional on \(\mathcal F_n\), the score is a linear transformation of the stipulated primitive Gaussian errors and is therefore jointly Gaussian with mean zero and this covariance.  Since \(X_n=\boldsymbol\vartheta_n(\varphi)+\boldsymbol G_{\mathrm{dir},n}\),
\[
 X_n\mid\mathcal F_n\sim
 N\bigl(\boldsymbol\vartheta_n(\varphi),\Sigma_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr).
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\boldsymbol 1_H\) and \(\boldsymbol h_n\) are linearly independent, so the curve indexed by \(\varphi\in[-\pi/6,\pi/6]\) is nonconstant; the covariance lower bound makes the experiment nondegenerate.  All defining conditions of \(\mathcal C_n\) have now been checked, proving \(\mathcal L_n\subset\mathcal C_n\) and all remaining assertions.
